newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-FIFA, KIRCH DENY WORLD CUP DEAL IN DANGER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FIFA, KIRCH DENY WORLD CUP DEAL IN DANGER.

text.p: Soccer's governing body FIFA and the Kirch Group of Germany on Friday denied press reports that the media giant was in danger of losing broadcasting rights to the 2002 and 2006 World Cups.

Several newspapers had reported that Kirch risked losing the television rights by signing a distribution contract with Prisma Sport & Media, a Swiss marketing agency, on the grounds that FIFA prohibits third-party deals.
Swiss company Sporis and Kirch unit TaurusFilm share the television rights to the two soccer championships, which have an estimated value of 3.4 billion marks ($1.9 billion).

"The fact is that Kirch has brought in a third firm without discussing it with its partners (FIFA and Sporis) which FIFA objects to," FIFA spokesman Keith Cooper told Reuters. "But it is not correct to say the contract is in danger."
Under an agreement sealed last year, Sporis and Kirch have worldwide broadcasting rights to the two tournaments, excluding the United States.

The Sueddeutsche Zeitung newspaper on Friday quoted a FIFA spokesman as saying that if Kirch and Sporis could not agree to a marketing scheme for the World Cup, "the whole agreement may need to be reexamined".

A Kirch Group spokesman said that it had hired Prisma to design its World Cup distribution strategy, coordinate plans with Sporis and arrange FIFA's approval, and said the deal did not violate its contract with FIFA and Sporis.
But Sporis's wholly-owned agency ISL said they backed FIFA's view that bringing in a third company needed the approval of both partners.
Cooper told Reuters that the partners planned to meet in the next few days to discuss the disagreement. ($ = 1.753 German Marks)
